profile.headline: Embedded & IoT Technical Lead | Firmware, RFID, Customer-Facing NPI | Product & Technical Leadership
profile.summary:
I've spent my career building things that live at the intersection of hardware and software — firmware for chemical detectors, retail security systems, industrial packaging machines, RFID readers, and thermal printers. The common thread is taking something from "we need this to exist" all the way through to "it's in a customer's hands and it works."
 
For the past decade I've also run my own embedded consulting firm, iOnyx, which taught me more about product delivery than any engineering role ever could. When you're scoping the engagement, writing the firmware, running it through Apple MFi certification, and on the hook when something breaks in the field — you learn very quickly what matters and what doesn't.
 
At Honeywell, I've led firmware and software delivery across a number of new-product-introduction programs over the years. My current focus is thermal management firmware — owning the subsystem architecture and coordinating across hardware, platform firmware, and test teams. I also lead cross-platform defect analysis and engineering change work across our printer portfolio — the kind of unsexy sustaining engineering that keeps products healthy in the field. Before shifting to printer firmware, I spent several years as RFID software lead for Honeywell's connected reader product lines, driving NPI delivery, edge-to-cloud architecture decisions, and customer pilots. Before Honeywell, I worked across the Charlotte tech scene at companies building everything from IoT security devices to defense detection systems.
 
I have an MSEE and a BS in Computer Engineering from UNC Charlotte, and I still write code most days — but the problems I'm most drawn to are the ones where technology, user needs, and business constraints all collide.
 
I'm most energized by roles that sit at that same hardware-software intersection — technical product leadership, embedded engineering management, or senior firmware positions where customer outcomes and technical depth both matter. Always open to a conversation.

positions.title: Senior Advanced Software Engineer
positions.description:
· Led SW/FW development for NPI RFID projects, managing resources, architecture design, and feature implementation (C, C#) for RFID stack integration, APIs, and proprietary logic. Drove cost reduction by porting modules to new MCUs and chipsets (C, FreeRTOS) and collaborated globally to meet timelines
· Automated testing and analysis with Python, reducing field defects and analysis time.
· Managed defect resolution and feature development (C, Embedded Linux) for thermal printers, consistently meeting deadlines and exceeding goals/quotas for defect resolution volume/timing.
· Designed and implemented RFID-based RTLS algorithms (C#)
· Supported customer-facing initiatives, including pilot installs, performance analysis, requirements gathering, and on-site testing.
· Provided driver support and defect resolution (C++) for radio interface on legacy mobility devices along with supporting WWAN certification efforts.

positions.title: President & Lead Design Engineer
positions.description:
· Worked directly with clients to create requirements and testing documentation to drive development.
· Implemented diverse features (C) across multiple microprocessors and platforms (Microchip, STM, Cypress, Nordic, FreeRTOS, Zephyr, Baremetal).
· Developed functionality such as custom iAP2 stack (including I2C driver for Apple Authentication Coprocessor), Bluetooth drivers, power optimization, custom bootloaders, NFC integration, and backend API architecture.
· Conducted extensive testing, including MFi certification, RF performance, signal integrity, and power profiling.
· Used Slack, JIRA, Trello, and Git for client communication, project management, and remote collaboration.

positions.title: Senior Electrical/Firmware Engineer
positions.description:
· Led redesign of inter-board communications layer (C) over CAN bus, improving reliability and reducing packet loss in industrial foam packaging machines.
· Developed lightweight bootloader (C) with field upgrade capabilities for control boards.
· Upgraded communications, UI, and features, and resolved defects in main control PC (C#).
· Resolved control board defects (C) within deadlines, documenting root cause analyses.
· Modified heating and motor control algorithms (C) to address defects in air packaging machines.

positions.title: Electrical/Firmware Engineer
positions.description:
· Designed firmware for TI, Freescale, Silicon Labs, Cypress, and Microchip microcontrollers (C) with ultra-low power and security features, including interrupt-driven architectures, MCU sleep modes, and data obfuscation.
· Led migration to agile processes and JIRA for issue tracking; used source control (Git, SVN).
· Developed algorithms and device simulation on TI MSP430 and Windows 10 IoT Core (C# on RPi).
· Implemented mobile applications with Bluetooth and USB (Windows 10, Android, iOS).
· Conducted low-level debugging with oscilloscope, multimeter, and logic analyzer.
· Contributed to product and software requirements; executed unit and system testing.

positions.title: Electrical/Firmware Engineer
positions.description:
· Developed firmware for Microchip microcontrollers (8, 16, 32 bit) with ultra-low power designs (interrupt-driven, sleep modes).
· Designed localization algorithm using angle of arrival data on Windows 7 Embedded (C# with TCPIP).
· Implemented motion detection filtering, device tracking, and status system architecture.
· Created drivers for LCD, MiWi radio, and accelerometer; utilized SPI, I2C, and UART for communication and debugging.
· Conducted low-level debugging, memory optimization, and timing/PWM setup; tested RF emissions with spectrum analyzer for compliance and performance.

positions.title: Associate Electrical/Firmware Engineer
positions.description:
· Designed firmware for Microchip (16 & 32 bit) MCUs, ported detection algorithm, and created control logic for Peltier cooler in detection systems.
· Resolved asynchronous counting issues in detection algorithms by modifying Xilinx CPLD logic.
· Developed embedded UI, graphics engine, and webserver for control and data analysis, including HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
· Implemented command parsers and utilized TCPIP, USB, and UART for external communication.
